title: Blue-green deployments
description: Run two identical production environments and switch traffic between them to eliminate downtime during releases.

data.text: Blue-green deployment is one of the oldest and most reliable zero-downtime release strategies. You maintain two identical production environments: blue runs the current live version, and green runs the new version. After you verify that green is healthy, you switch all traffic from blue to green. If something goes wrong, you switch back instantly.

The strategy is simple in concept but requires careful planning around databases, caches, and external integrations. This lesson explains when blue-green deployments shine, what infrastructure they require, and how to avoid the hidden costs of running duplicate production capacity.

data.title: Blue-green steps
items: Blue environment serves all live traffic.
Green environment receives the new release and is tested independently.
Health checks confirm green is stable.
A load balancer or DNS switch redirects traffic from blue to green.
Blue is kept running for a safety window, then scaled down.

data.text: Blue-green deployments require enough capacity to run two full production environments simultaneously. In cloud platforms, this often means doubling the number of App Service instances, virtual machines, or containers during the transition. For large applications, this cost can be significant, so many teams reserve blue-green for major releases rather than every commit.

data.title: Watch the database
data.text: If the new version changes the database schema, both blue and green must be compatible with the same data. Use backward-compatible schema changes or separate databases with replication. A shared database couples the two environments and defeats the purpose.

data.title: Good fits
items: Major version upgrades where rollback speed is critical.
UI redesigns that need instant user-facing rollback.
Regulated environments that require proven backout plans.

data.title: Poor fits
items: High-traffic systems that cannot afford double the compute cost.
Stateful applications with complex session affinity requirements.
Teams without automated smoke tests to validate the green environment.

cards.title: Blue-green
cards.description: Two full environments; traffic switches atomically.

cards.title: Rolling update
cards.description: Replace instances gradually while keeping service available.

data.title: Key takeaways
points: Blue-green gives instant rollback by preserving the old environment.
The database is the hardest part; keep schema changes backward compatible.
Use it for high-risk releases where speed of rollback matters more than cost.
Verify the green environment with automated smoke tests before switching traffic.
data.takeaway: Blue-green trades infrastructure cost for safety and speed of recovery.

items.question: Does blue-green require zero-downtime DNS?
items.answer: Not necessarily. A load balancer or traffic manager can switch instantly. DNS-based switches are slower and harder to roll back because of caching.

items.question: How long should I keep the old environment running?
items.answer: Keep blue available until you are confident green is stable. Many teams wait one business cycle, such as 24 hours, before decommissioning blue.
